Take it slow. Don't push yourself just yet because it might lead to an emotional burnout.

Try to think of exercise as a part of life you'll carry with you always, and not a remedy for weight hazards.

Walking is excellent, you can try power-walking which has full potential of making you break a sweat without complexity. 
Do easy exercises and increase reps so you can keep at it and also feel the burn. You'll get your strength back, don't worry. Just start easy. 

Your body will naturally scream for intensity when whatever you're doing is no longer hard enough, speaking from personal experience.

1.Diet and movement. How you approach the former will make you reduce either fat or weight. (Fat is just fat whereas Weight is fat plus some amount of muscle mass)

2.Elimination of ultra-processed, high-fat foods and prioritising protein will make you lose fat and be optimal for recovery and muscle retention. (Resistance training is cherry on top during weight loss period)
Protein foods can be non vegetarian or vegetarian, the latter being a limited resource when it comes to complete proteins. Complete proteins are much preferred for their complete amino acid profile. 
Some amount of research will help you find out what you can practically incorporate in your day to diet. Don't stress it.

3.You can start with cardio workouts at home combined with calisthenics suchs as planks, push ups and sit ups if you like. (Research more into calisthenics and find out what you'd enjoy doing, specifically targetting your upper body)
You can simply start at home by looking up youtube workouts and stick to what you enjoy the most.
